Class AABB

java.lang.Object
geometries.api.AABB
public class AABB extends Object
An Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB): the smallest box, with faces parallel to the X/Y/Z planes, that fully encloses a geometry or a group of geometries.

This is the core primitive of the BVH (Bounding Volume Hierarchy) acceleration. A ray-box test is far cheaper than a ray-geometry test, so if a ray misses the box it cannot possibly hit anything inside it, and the expensive geometry test is skipped (this is the CBR — Conservative Bounding Region — optimization).

The box is immutable. Unbounded geometries (such as an infinite plane or tube) use INFINITE, a box that every ray intersects, so they are never wrongly pruned.

  • Method Details

    • intersects

      public boolean intersects(Ray ray)
      Tests whether a ray intersects this box, using the classic "slab" method: for each axis the box is a slab between two parallel planes; the ray hits the box only if its entry/exit intervals on all three axes overlap.
      Parameters:
      ray - the ray to test
      Returns:
      true if the ray meets the box (or starts inside it)

    • union

      public AABB union(AABB other)
      Returns the smallest box that contains both this box and another — used when building a hierarchy node from its children.
      Parameters:
      other - the other box
      Returns:
      the union (combined) box

    • isFinite

      public boolean isFinite()
      Reports whether this is a real, finite box (as opposed to INFINITE). Unbounded geometries (plane, tube) produce an infinite box and must be kept out of the spatial tree, since they have no meaningful center to sort by.
      Returns:
      true if all six bounds are finite
